text: This November, Iran erased a line it had kept for years.
2,000 km. The farthest its missiles were meant to fly.
Inside it: Israel, the Gulf, and every American base in the region.
In March, during the war, two missiles flew toward Diego Garcia, about 4,000 km away.
Britain says one failed, and one was shot down. Iran denies firing them.
Now its Revolutionary Guard says the limit is gone.
But Washington is 10,000 km from Tehran.
That takes an intercontinental missile, and Iran is not known to have one.
US intelligence says it could build one by 2035, if it decides to.
The line is gone. The distance isn't.
